title: Accessing & managing financial data

**Exercises:**

1. Read the book chapters [Accessing and managing financial data](https://www.tidy-finance.org/chapters/accessing-and-managing-financial-data.html) and [WRDS, CRSP, and Compustat](https://www.tidy-finance.org/chapters/wrds-crsp-and-compustat.html) entirely; both show the R and the Python code side by side. They may contain some advanced concepts but also a description of almost every important dataset relevant to research in empirical finance. Since CRSP's update in July 2022, monthly returns already include delisting returns, so you no longer need to adjust for delistings yourself; the second chapter explains the details.

2. Fill the `data` folder of your course repository. It starts empty; R and Python read the same files from it, as in the book. Git ignores everything in it, so none of the files ends up on GitHub.

    a. *Public data:* download the Fama-French factors, the industry portfolios, the macroeconomic predictors, and the consumer price index with `tidyfinance`, and store them as parquet files. The code below does what the chapter *Accessing and managing financial data* does; run it once from the course repository.

    b. *Proprietary data:* download `crsp_monthly.parquet` and `beta.parquet` from Absalon and store them in the `data` folder as well. Later in the course, `stock_characteristics_monthly.parquet` follows the same way.

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}
## Python

```{python}
#| label: py-download-public-data
#| eval: false
import polars as pl
import tidyfinance as tf

start_date = "1960-01-01"
end_date = "2024-12-31"

factors_ff3_monthly = tf.download_data(
    domain="Fama-French",
    dataset="Fama/French 3 Factors",
    start_date=start_date,
    end_date=end_date,
)

factors_ff5_monthly = tf.download_data(
    domain="Fama-French",
    dataset="Fama/French 5 Factors (2x3)",
    start_date=start_date,
    end_date=end_date,
)

factors_ff3_daily = tf.download_data(
    domain="Fama-French",
    dataset="Fama/French 3 Factors [Daily]",
    start_date=start_date,
    end_date=end_date,
)

industries_ff_monthly = tf.download_data(
    domain="Fama-French",
    dataset="10 Industry Portfolios",
    start_date=start_date,
    end_date=end_date,
)

macro_predictors = tf.download_data(
    domain="Goyal-Welch",
    dataset="monthly",
    start_date=start_date,
    end_date=end_date,
)

cpi_monthly = (
    tf.download_data(
        domain="FRED",
        series="CPIAUCNS",
        start_date=start_date,
        end_date=end_date,
    )
    .sort("date")
    .with_columns(cpi=pl.col("value") / pl.col("value").last())
)

data_dict = {
    "factors_ff3_monthly": factors_ff3_monthly,
    "factors_ff5_monthly": factors_ff5_monthly,
    "factors_ff3_daily": factors_ff3_daily,
    "industries_ff_monthly": industries_ff_monthly,
    "macro_predictors": macro_predictors,
    "cpi_monthly": cpi_monthly,
}

for name, data in data_dict.items():
    data.write_parquet(f"data/{name}.parquet")
```

## R

```{r}
#| label: r-download-public-data
#| eval: false
library(tidyverse)
library(tidyfinance)
library(nanoparquet)

start_date <- "1960-01-01"
end_date <- "2024-12-31"

factors_ff3_monthly <- download_data(
  domain = "Fama-French",
  dataset = "Fama/French 3 Factors",
  start_date = start_date,
  end_date = end_date
)

factors_ff5_monthly <- download_data(
  domain = "Fama-French",
  dataset = "Fama/French 5 Factors (2x3)",
  start_date = start_date,
  end_date = end_date
)

factors_ff3_daily <- download_data(
  domain = "Fama-French",
  dataset = "Fama/French 3 Factors [Daily]",
  start_date = start_date,
  end_date = end_date
)

industries_ff_monthly <- download_data(
  domain = "Fama-French",
  dataset = "10 Industry Portfolios",
  start_date = start_date,
  end_date = end_date
)

macro_predictors <- download_data(
  domain = "Goyal-Welch",
  dataset = "monthly",
  start_date = start_date,
  end_date = end_date
)

cpi_monthly <- download_data(
  domain = "FRED",
  series = "CPIAUCNS",
  start_date = start_date,
  end_date = end_date
) |>
  mutate(cpi = value / value[date == max(date)])

lst(
  factors_ff3_monthly,
  factors_ff5_monthly,
  factors_ff3_daily,
  industries_ff_monthly,
  macro_predictors,
  cpi_monthly
) |>
  iwalk(\(data, name) write_parquet(data, paste0("data/", name, ".parquet")))
```

:::

3. Almost all exercises from now on start with reading data from these files, so make sure you familiarize yourself with this short *minimal setup to load data into your R or Python session memory from a fresh session* (you can consult it anytime again later during the course).

::: {.panel-tabset group="language"}
## Python

```{python}
#| label: py-load-crsp-monthly
#| eval: false
import polars as pl

crsp_monthly = pl.read_parquet("data/crsp_monthly.parquet")
```

## R

```{r}
#| label: r-load-crsp-monthly
#| eval: false
library(nanoparquet)

crsp_monthly <- read_parquet("data/crsp_monthly.parquet")
```

:::
